what_happened: The retry job "store failure lines, not CI cleanup, in failed-check tail" was rejected at the final verdict. This is the fix for the problem seen in the earlier jobs 20261106-042824-j07h and 20261106-022422-jkfa, where failed-check output was only CI cleanup. Two of 7 acceptance criteria were unmet. The first: a test in gh/tests.rs with a failing test followed by a cleanup block must assert that output_tail holds the FAILED/panicked lines and no cleanup text. The second: a test with a panic message longer than 4 lines must assert the whole message survives. There were three blocker or major findings. Two say that behavior criteria 2 and 4 cite no commands that ran (D43). The third says finding 2 from the earlier attempt is still not fixed: a failure block is still the marker plus at most 4 lines (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs:209,274), and no test covers a longer panic message. No checks failed. The unmet criteria are the two test criteria. The failed-check list is empty.
cause: I chose this class by closest fit, but it is a loose match. The registry has no class for "criterion requires evidence in the producer's report that the verifier must then check." Class 20261027-011728-xrka comes close, but this case has a real code gap as well, so I did not use it. The D43 rule that behavior-criterion evidence must cite commands that ran is checked only by the verifier at the end. The producer is not told to record the exact commands and their results in a form the verifier can read. The retry also carried over the earlier finding (the 4-line cap on a failure block) only as prose. Nothing turned it into a failing test that the producer had to make pass before finishing. So the work was judged once, at the final verdict, and the same gaps came back after a retry.
prevention: Add a pre-verdict check that runs after the producer finishes. For each behavior criterion it requires a recorded command and exit status, and it re-runs the named test commands itself. If a named test is missing or not run, the producer gets one repair round before the verifier is called. On a retry, the earlier verifier findings are turned into explicit criteria. Here that would be "a failure block keeps the whole panic message, not the marker plus 4 lines". Those criteria are named test commands that must run and pass.
proposed_request: Fix the failed-check output tail in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs so it holds the failing test lines and not CI cleanup text. Outcome: when a test check fails, the stored output_tail contains each FAILED line and each full `panicked at` message, however many lines the message has (remove the cap of 4 lines after the marker). It must contain no post-job cleanup text such as git config includeIf removal, orphan process cleanup or Node.js deprecation warnings. Acceptance: (1) A test in the gh tests (detail_from_job_logs) feeds a log with a failing test followed by a cleanup block and asserts output_tail has the FAILED and panicked lines and none of the cleanup text. It must fail on the base and pass after the change. (2) A test feeds a panic message longer than 4 lines and asserts the whole message is in output_tail. (3) Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`. In the report, list each command you ran and its pass or fail result for every behavior criterion, as D43 requires. (4) If the change touches code that docs/decisions.md records a decision for, append an amending or confirming entry at the end of the log and do not edit existing lines. Context: the earlier attempt 20261106-191125-zy9w left the 4-line cap in place and had no test for a longer panic message.
